case_name: Robert O. Edwards, Jr. v. Douglas A. Collins
court: United States Court of Appeals for Veterans Claims

issues.label: Board jurisdiction under AMA
issues.why: The court must confirm it has authority to review the August 5, 2024 Board decision under the AMA framework.

issues.label: Standard of judicial review
issues.why: The court must apply the correct standards (e.g., clearly erroneous factfinding, de novo legal questions, reasons-or-bases adequacy, and prejudicial error).

issues.label: Scope of record on review
issues.why: The court must determine what materials the Board was legally permitted or required to consider given the direct review docket.

issues.label: Direct review record-closure rule
issues.why: The court must assess whether 38 U.S.C. § 7113(a) barred the Board from considering Update 2012 because it was not in the AOJ record.

issues.label: Update 2012 as argument
issues.why: The court must decide whether the Board erred by refusing to consider the claimant’s citation to Update 2012 as legal/medical argument even if the document itself was not in the record.

issues.label: Constructive possession doctrine
issues.why: The court must decide whether NAS Update 2012 was constructively before the AOJ/Board despite not being physically in the claims file at the time of the AOJ decision.

issues.label: Constructive possession prerequisites
issues.why: The court must address whether the NAS report was generated/controlled by VA, reasonably expected to be connected to the claim, and relevant such that constructive possession applies.

issues.label: AMA vs constructive possession
issues.why: The court must resolve how constructive possession interacts with AMA record-closure provisions and whether § 7113(a) limits that doctrine.

issues.label: Duty-to-assist timing
issues.why: The court must determine whether any duty-to-assist error occurred at the AOJ stage (where AMA permits remand for predecisional errors) rather than at the Board stage.

issues.label: Predecisional duty-to-assist remand
issues.why: The court must decide whether the Board was required to remand for correction of any predecisional duty-to-assist error, including failure to obtain an exam or relevant evidence.

issues.label: Duty to obtain federal records
issues.why: The court must consider whether 38 U.S.C. § 5103A required VA to obtain and consider NAS reports as relevant federal/public records.

issues.label: Duty to consider NAS reports
issues.why: The court must decide whether VA must address NAS Updates in herbicide-exposure cancer claims even when the disease is not presumptive.

issues.label: McLendon exam entitlement
issues.why: The court must decide whether the low-threshold criteria under 38 U.S.C. § 5103A(d)(2) were met to require a VA medical examination/opinion.

issues.label: Current disability element
issues.why: The court must ensure the Board properly found (or addressed) whether squamous cell carcinoma of the right tonsil is a current disability or residual disability.

issues.label: In-service event/exposure
issues.why: The court must confirm whether herbicide exposure in Vietnam was conceded or otherwise established as an in-service event.

issues.label: Nexus element framework
issues.why: The court must ensure the Board applied the correct direct-service-connection elements (Washington v. Nicholson) rather than presumptive rules.

issues.label: Indication of association evidence
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether the submitted prior Board decisions and/or NAS Updates were sufficient to ‘indicate’ a possible nexus for exam purposes.

issues.label: Competency of prior Board decisions
issues.why: The court must decide the legal effect of other Board decisions under 38 C.F.R. § 20.1303 and whether they can trigger duty-to-assist development.

issues.label: Board’s analogy/distinguish rationale
issues.why: The court must assess whether the Board adequately explained why the cited 2015 Board decisions were not analogous or persuasive.

issues.label: Reasons-or-bases adequacy
issues.why: The court must determine whether the Board provided an adequate statement of reasons or bases for all material findings, including the exam denial.

issues.label: Addressing favorable evidence
issues.why: The court must decide whether the Board failed to discuss potentially favorable evidence (e.g., biological-mechanism theory referenced in submitted materials).

issues.label: NAS categorization significance
issues.why: The court must consider what legal weight ‘inadequate/insufficient evidence’ in NAS Updates carries for direct service connection and for triggering an exam.

issues.label: Reliance on negative NAS evidence
issues.why: The court must address whether NAS’s ‘insufficient evidence’ category was misused as affirmative negative evidence against nexus.

issues.label: Medical complexity and expertise
issues.why: The court must consider whether the nexus question required medical expertise such that the Board could not reject an exam without adequate medical basis.

issues.label: Lay evidence of infection theory
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether the claimant’s assertions about infection leading to tonsillar cancer were competent, credible, and relevant to the exam threshold.

issues.label: Raising Update 2010 via submission
issues.why: The court must decide whether the April 2015 Board decision’s discussion of Update 2010 effectively raised Update 2010’s contents before the AOJ as part of the record.

issues.label: Whether Update 2010 was in record
issues.why: The court must determine factually/legalistically whether Update 2010 was constructively or actually before the AOJ on March 26, 2020.

issues.label: Board’s treatment of Update 2010
issues.why: The court must decide whether the Board erred by not discussing Update 2010 while discussing materials that referenced it.

issues.label: AOJ failure to list NAS in evidence
issues.why: The court must consider whether the AOJ’s omission of NAS reports from its evidence summary reflects a failure to consider relevant material or a duty-to-assist error.

issues.label: Higher-level review constraints
issues.why: The court must account for what evidence and development is permitted during higher-level review and whether failure to address NAS/exam was erroneous there.

issues.label: Board’s legal error on record bar
issues.why: The court must decide whether the Board’s statement that it could not consider Update 2012 ‘as argument or evidence’ was legally correct.

issues.label: Harmless error / prejudice
issues.why: The court must determine whether any error (record scope, constructive possession, exam denial, reasons-or-bases) was prejudicial and could have affected the outcome.

issues.label: Appropriate remedy scope
issues.why: The court must decide whether remand instructions should require obtaining/considering NAS reports, providing an exam, or re-adjudicating under correct legal standards.

issues.label: Limits on court factfinding
issues.why: The court must ensure it does not engage in prohibited factfinding and instead remands for necessary factual determinations by the Board/AOJ.

issues.label: Secretary’s litigation position
issues.why: The court must evaluate any post hoc rationalizations versus the Board’s stated reasons and confine review to the Board’s rationale.
